lessons: Avoid starting with declarative exposition like 'When maple trees wake up in spring...', as it caused the largest single drop (-38.5%) across the analyzed videos.
Do not include meta-engagement prompts like 'Pause and guess...', which triggered an immediate 15.4% drop in retention.
Frame the hook as an unresolved paradox or sensory tension (e.g., trying to fix spicy food with ice water) to achieve strong 10% retention above 1.0 despite weak relative starts.
Keep initial explanations punchy; high drops consistently occur between 10% and 26% of video length when pacing slows down.
Not enough data to establish a definitive rule for countdowns, as none were present in the analyzed sample.
worst_moment_types: Expository scientific setup statements ('When maple trees wake up in spring...')
Meta-commentary and direct interaction prompts ('Pause and guess...')
Slow transitions or elaborations between the 10% and 26% marks
best_hook_types: Conflict-driven hooks that highlight a failed everyday solution ('Gulping ice water... but the real fire stays untouched')
Intriguing everyday phenomena that promise a hidden mechanism ('Why your eyes are secretly leaking', 'Why Onions Make You Cry')
